_comment: Single source for /map-sources (React page src/components/MapSourcesPage.tsx + SSR seo/render-map-sources.js). releases[].ids are the PMTiles `version` values (= release dates); identical releases are grouped, each id gets its own anchor. releases[0] is the CURRENT release. intro.en: The satellite imagery of the basemap (layers `land`, `coast`, `coast14`) is cut to land with a land/water mask. The mask is derived from OpenStreetMap data and is therefore a Derivative Database under the [Open Database License 1.0](https://opendatacommons.org/licenses/odbl/1-0/). As required by section 4.6, this is the method by which anyone can rebuild it from the same inputs. The method is offered under ODbL 1.0.
intro.pl: Zdjęcia satelitarne mapy podkładowej (warstwy `land`, `coast`, `coast14`) są przycinane do lądu maską ląd/woda. Maska jest wyprowadzona z danych OpenStreetMap, więc jest bazą pochodną (Derivative Database) w rozumieniu [Open Database License 1.0](https://opendatacommons.org/licenses/odbl/1-0/). Zgodnie z sekcją 4.6 poniżej opisano metodę, którą każdy może odtworzyć maskę z tych samych danych wejściowych. Metoda jest udostępniona na licencji ODbL 1.0.
intro.de: Die Satellitenbilder der Basiskarte (Ebenen `land`, `coast`, `coast14`) werden mit einer Land-/Wasser-Maske auf das Land zugeschnitten. Die Maske ist aus OpenStreetMap-Daten abgeleitet und damit eine abgeleitete Datenbank (Derivative Database) nach der [Open Database License 1.0](https://opendatacommons.org/licenses/odbl/1-0/). Wie in Abschnitt 4.6 gefordert, beschreibt dies die Methode, mit der jeder sie aus denselben Eingangsdaten nachbauen kann. Die Methode wird unter ODbL 1.0 angeboten.
intro.fr: L'imagerie satellite du fond de carte (couches `land`, `coast`, `coast14`) est découpée sur la terre à l'aide d'un masque terre/eau. Le masque est dérivé des données OpenStreetMap et constitue donc une base de données dérivée (Derivative Database) au sens de l'[Open Database License 1.0](https://opendatacommons.org/licenses/odbl/1-0/). Comme l'exige la section 4.6, voici la méthode permettant à chacun de le reconstruire à partir des mêmes données d'entrée. La méthode est proposée sous ODbL 1.0.

items: OpenStreetMap land polygons (derived from the OSM coastline), taken from the [Overture Maps](https://docs.overturemaps.org/attribution/) base theme, release `2026-10-21.0`, `type=land`, `subtype=land`, `class=land` (all selected rows have `sources.dataset = OpenStreetMap`). © OpenStreetMap contributors, [ODbL](https://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright).

Copernicus Sentinel-2 imagery, green (B03) and near-infrared (B08) bands: Sentinel-2 Level 3 quarterly mosaics 2025 from the [Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem](https://dataspace.copernicus.eu/) (for 139 Arctic tiles the summer of another year, 2021–2026).

method.text: **Steps (per map tile, in Web Mercator, EPSG:3857)**

items: Rasterise the OSM land polygons to the tile grid (anti-aliased, 2× supersampling): OSM land = 1, sea = 0.
Compute NDWI = (green − NIR) / (green + NIR) from the imagery. Map it to a soft "not water" value: 1 at NDWI ≤ −0.05, 0 at NDWI ≥ 0.10, linear in between.

Keep that image-derived "not water" only within 1,000 m seaward of OSM land (distance measured to the nearest OSM land pixel, including OSM land in neighbouring tiles). Further out to sea it is ignored.

Final mask = maximum of step 1 and step 3. So the mask is OSM land plus what the image shows as not water close to the OSM coastline: piers, breakwaters, harbour moles, sandbanks and coastline changes newer than OSM.
Light smoothing of the image-derived part (Gaussian, σ = 0.8 px) so the edge is not jagged.

Low zooms only (z8–11, layer `land`): the mask is eroded by one pixel, so the coarse coastline stays inside the sharper coastline of the z12–14 layers. Pixels set back to water by step 7 count as land for this erosion only (they stay water), so thin OSM land beside them is not eroded away.

Dark sea read as land is removed from step 3: a connected patch inside the 1 km zone and outside OSM land is set back to water when its mean NIR reflectance is below 0.03, at most 10% of its pixels exceed 0.12, its mean red reflectance is at most 0.026, and no bright (cloud-like) pixel, blue > 0.20, lies within 300 m. The patch is widened by one pixel before it is cleared, so no faint rim of the soft edge remains.

method.text: **Not part of the mask:** the imagery itself, GEBCO bathymetry and the place-name labels.
The mask is not a product of its own and is not published as a file; this description is the offer under ODbL 4.6. Questions: through the contact on [something-rare.com](https://something-rare.com/).
